messages.content: I need all pending and active mandates of users parath and bhanu

function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.reasoning:
We need to call user_mandates twice: one for parath, one for bhanu. But we need both pending and active mandates. The function signature allows specifying status: "active" or "pending". It doesn't allow multiple statuses at once. So we need to call twice per user? Actually we can call with status "active" and then "pending" separately. Or we could call partner_mandates with status unspecified to get all, but that would return all mandates for the partner, not just for those two users. We want only for parath and bhanu. So we need to call user_mandates twice per user? That would be four calls. But maybe we can call user_mandates with status unspecified (default active) for each user, then call again with status pending. So total four calls.

But maybe we can combine? The function doesn't support multiple names. So we need separate calls. So we should do:

Call user_mandates({"name":"parath"}) -> active mandates for parath.

Call user_mandates({"name":"parath","status":"pending"}) -> pending mandates for parath.

Similarly for bhanu.

Thus four calls. Let's do them sequentially. We'll output the results.
